Implications of Blockchain Technology in the Tourism Sector

Many advantages of blockchain can be utilized in the protection of the ICH. The appeal and beauty of BCT are further bolstered by its underlying concepts and guiding ideals. They include 1) a distributed ledger format that gives each system member access to a “public” record of transactions, 2) a distributed consensus, wherein all participants concur that the records are accurate and genuine, 3) immutability since each participant is a component of the structure and is unable to operate on their own, 4) provenance, as each transaction has a digital history that can be tracked and validated as to its provenance, characteristics, and ownership and 5) native cryptography since the blockchain has strong security features built in to keep unauthorized intruders out. The hospitality services and tourism sector, like other sectors, is constantly looking for cutting-edge solutions to assist boosting competitive edge, elevate customer fulfilment, and enhance bottom-line performance. To this aim, the lodging, travel agency, and food service industries can strategically use blockchain to achieve this purpose. Other benefits of using Blockchain for the travel agency/agent industry include, but are not restricted to 1) secure transfer and sharing of client/passenger information, 2) online dependability, 3) better transaction security, and 4) the effective mitigation of lost or stolen records and transactions. Tourism is heavily reliant on culture, current conditions, and historical events. Any site can attract tourists thanks to its unique cultural experiences, so it is essential to protect that heritage to preserve its legacy.

Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) and Digitalization

The valuation of cultural heritage is derived from its authenticity, quality, and intangible values. These elements contribute to the cultural asset's uniqueness and non-replicability. Digitization has created intriguing threats to cultural heritage authentication because it can be conveniently modified, recreated, and distributed at low cost if not properly managed (Gipp et al., 2017). Technology enables us to overcome issues concerning the authenticity and origins of works and ethnic content. As Angelova (2019) proposes, blockchain may be utilized to create an unchanging registration that contains the form and categorization of cultural property, as well as all activities performed and authorised on cultural heritage assets. The preservation of documentary heritage must be considered in terms of organising what we did inherit from the history in such a way that we can all give it over to the coming years. Documentary protection makes perfect sense only when we take responsibility for the preservation of objects, built-in environments, and landscapes. Digitization is now a matter of practicality and reality, with technological interventions providing improved access to data resources, preservation, and dissemination as needed, at any time and from any location. This research contributes much to the discussion of blockchain's potential applications in heritage conservation by outlining a path toward further disintermediation. It also adds to the ongoing conversation on the qualities and advantages of blockchain technology as they pertain to safeguarding intangible cultural treasures. Finding ways to preserve our cultural heritage through digital preservation of resources. If the manuscripts are digitised and made available on the internet, they will be easily available from anywhere in the world, and users will not need to travel to the locations where the documents are physically preserved. The significance of digital preservation could be overstated. Culture and heritage are valuable legacies that all people share across national boundaries and must be passed on to succeeding generations.

Blockchain technology provides a method for linking intangible cultural assets with science, tourism, and heritage preservation (Shuai & Yu, 2021). One of the greatest ways to put the concept into practice is with the use of blockchain technology, which can also be utilised to better protect the ICH travel experiences (Hu et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2018) as stated by Anagnostakis (2019). The introduction of Blockchain in cultural heritage documentation will provide an invaluable, universal, and immune timeline of cultural heritage documentation records, safeguarding the validity of data and the value of tokens and facilitating in the most effective way the resolution of ownership and enhancement problems for future generations.

If the blockchain strategy is properly used, it can be used to a degree that has yet to be investigated. An exceedingly delicate and successful strategy for drawing tourists to India's culturally extraordinarily rich country is the preservation of its intangible cultural heritage. In this process, blockchain technology could be an extremely helpful tool. When examining the benefits and repercussions of blockchain for the tourism industry, it becomes abundantly evident that this technology has the potential to advance the concept of intangible cultural heritage (Panasiuk, 2021).

Blockchain can be incorporated into the ICH tourism sector for encrypted data storage about the various ICH practices and performances (Pozzi & Katos, 2017). For booking lodging, services, and ICH items in several locations, blockchain can offer a very safe platform. At ICH destinations, blockchain can be employed as a carrier of protected tourist data and procedures. For safe payment methods like cryptocurrencies and other flexible payment options at ICH locations, blockchain can be suggested. Blockchain technology may be used as a strategy to win over tourists to an ICH destination by ensuring that services are delivered in a secure manner. The blockchain's core characteristics can be utilised to deduce other attributes. One of the most important is (dispersed) trust, or the replacement of faith in people or organisations with trust in blockchain-based systems where information is immutably stored while algorithms are automatically performed out However, care must be taken to prevent erroneously believing that BCT can solve every trust-related issue. Potential problems include programming errors, malicious network intrusions, or powerful entities working behind the scenes to affect events (Degbey & Pelto, 2021). Another advantage of utilising asymmetric encryption is that data may be encrypted and decrypted using a pair of keys, which ensures authenticity. A so-called public key could be given to anyone, unlike a private key, which must be safeguarded by the owner. To decrypt a communication that has been encrypted, only the pair's first key can be utilised. Encryption algorithm can be employed for both confidentiality and authentication. This is accomplished by simply adding a private key to a message. Anyone who possesses the corresponding public key can immediately determine that a specific transaction might only have been made by the owner of the corresponding private key (Dubey et al., 2022; Treiblmaier, 2020).

Blockchain Technology and Indian ICH Preservation

The diverse and everlasting culture that has been passed down through the generations in India is without a doubt the most significant contribution that the country has made to the rest of the globe. This account of history includes almost the entirety of mankind's search for knowledge. This history is presently spread out among several different archival collections as well as private collections. Cultural heritage sites must respond and adapt to shifting contexts in a coherent manner, that is, in a way that is consistent with the memory and character of the place, in order to stay alive and relevant. The long-term viability of urban cultural assets can be negatively impacted by incoherent changes or transformations that, in the opinion of the local community, are not consistent with the character of a place (Roszczynska-Kurasinska et al., 2021). Since UNESCO first explicitly recommended protecting ICH in 2003, it really has progressively gained academics' attention and sparked lively academic debates. The aforementioned works have concentrated on the digital gathering, archiving, and presentation of particular kinds of ICH. The utilisation of digital technology (such as databases and motion capture technology) and digital presentation techniques have been the key topics of discussion (such as serious game design and interactive narratives). The monitoring of digital data over a period of time is known as digital preservation. It consists of procedures and operations that ensure ongoing access to data and all types of digital data, both technological and cultural heritage. The goal of digital conserving is long-term, error-free repository of digital information with retrieval and interpretation capabilities for the duration of the information's requirement. The subjects of ICH exhibitions are people and activities. Designers must interact with ICH's inheritors and communities, enter their lives, and gather new information on ICH. They must also take into account moral dilemmas and challenges with value orientations (Kong & Zhang, 2021).

Unfortunately, many aspects of India's physical past have been mutilated and obliterated as a result of some invasions; furthermore, some of this history is continually being taken, and books and manuscripts are degrading. The maintenance and protection of Indian culture is a challenging endeavour (Ruhanen & Whitford, 2019). The excellent thing is that the rapidly developing information technology field may be able to provide not just a resolution for preservation but also for enhancement and increased accessibility. The bad news is that information technology hasn't advanced very quickly. If Indian libraries digitised and disseminated their vast, ancient, and timeless cultural heritage, it might have a significant impact on the rest of the globe. The Indian government has started developing national policies and initiatives to protect the rich cultural legacy of the nation. Since these unique works of art are housed in so many different institutions across the nation, it is the duty of every individual library, museum, and archive to embrace digital preservation techniques to guarantee their accessibility in the future. A new analysis of the relevance, importance, and advantages to society and the global community of many of the initiatives currently being carried out by a range of organisations, institutions, and people all over the country of India is required (Sarabia-Molina et al., 2022). Because it gives us a tangible connection to our past and a sense of who we are as a people, cultural heritage preservation is vital to the success of the tourism industry. Art contributes to the preservation of culture, along with language, music, and craft, through the inheritance of traditions (Singh, 2022). In light of recent developments in information technology, it is critical to give serious consideration to the use of technologies such as blockchain for the preservation of cultural heritage to offer an additional layer of safety.

CONCLUSION

Thanks to the fast-paced growth of IT, digital protection of ICH is making strides in India and elsewhere, with more significant ICHs adopting this strategy. Research into digital security at the worldwide level is driven by three key areas: digital acquisition, digital preservation, and digital development. From the point of view of managing and utilizing digital information, research into digital protection focuses primarily on three facets: digital information organization, retrieval, and administration. The proliferation of connected devices and the Internet, however, has led to an explosion in the volume of data available online.

Despite its usefulness, the exchange of such vast amounts of data also poses security concerns. As the ICH continues to digitize its resources, more and more of those resources will become available online. Cyberspace poses a security concern for digital data. The preservation of digital information resources is a new concern that has arisen as a result of ICH's digitization (Bilgiçli, 2021). Integrity and encryption of ICH's digital information resources based on blockchain technology have been the topic of several investigations. The tourist industry is only one of several that might benefit from the increased disintermediation made possible by blockchain technology. The business model, monetary transfer mechanisms, security, performance, trustworthiness, etc. of the travel industry might all be affected by this technology (Latifi et al., 2021). Digitization projects involving artifacts from other cultures, rare literature, and historical archives have sparked interest in conducting digital studies across a wider range of disciplines. Currently, India should compete significantly with other Asian governments, such as China, in researching the implications of blockchain technology for ICH protection.

DISCUSSION

There are benefits to using block technology for the digital security of ICH. Comprehensively evaluating the digital preservation of ICH is one way to better achieve the transformation and inheritance of ICH information resources. This includes looking at it from the viewpoints of government policy direction, market deployment, and social support. The beneficial effects that blockchain technology may have present a promising option for the preservation of historical records. Researchers will profit from this study by learning more about the features and advantages of blockchain technology and how they might be used for the preservation of cultural artifacts as well as intangible cultural heritage. Blockchain can be included in models of heritage conservation to lessen the need for middlemen and encourage new entries into the field.

LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE RECOMMENDATIONS

This chapter is based on secondary data and a critical study of the same. We only considered papers published after 2010 when compiling our sources, and we limited ourselves to the Google Scholar database. Future research utilising a different methodology could be able to address the problems we encountered. A deep study using primary data from various stakeholders and a different quantitative or qualitative approach for the study of the implications can be done in the future for more enhanced and calculated results.

The current study stresses mainly on advantages of using blockchain in ICH enhancement and preservation, including how it will improve corporate operations, the standard of offered goods and services, data handling and security, as well as the national economy. However, several experts in other domains contend that blockchain technology itself has several security flaws. Future studies should therefore look into the main difficulties or disadvantages presented by blockchain technology and analyse their implications for ICH conservation using blockchain technology.

Blockchain is an emerging technology and has gained trust in the world of tech in no time. Data is the most important asset for any organization or institute as it holds the base of all information. Every now and then, cases of data leaking, piracy, and stealing could be found in many companies, businesses, industries, and markets ruining the database and causing hindrance to growth. This is where blockchain acts as a savior for these business and industrial organizations by protecting their data and transactions. Blockchain is a method of recording and handling data that makes it tough for the system to be altered, hacked, or manipulated by illegal sources. “Block” of public or the “chain” is the assembly that keeps transactional records which is connected by peer-to-peer nodes. This storage is also known as a “digital ledger.” It can be defined as a distributed ledger that replicates and allocates the transactions across the network of computers contributing to the blockchain.

KINDS OF BLOCKCHAIN

These are of four kinds:

  • • Public blockchain.
  • • Private blockchain.
  • • Hybrid blockchain.
  • • Consortium blockchain.

Public Blockchain

These type of blockchains are completely amenable to implement the decentralization concept. Anybody with a computer and internet access can connect the network; there is no limitations. This blockchain is available for every user because its name is public, which infers it is not measured by anyone. Anyone with internet access and a computer equipped with adequate hardware can participate in this blockchain shown in Figure 2.

Nodes or network blocks are copies of themselves on every machine in the network. We can also carry out transaction or record verification on this open blockchain.

Figure 2. Public blockchain network

Advantages

  • • Trustworthy: Algorithms exist to identify any scam. Participants don't need to worry about the additional nodes in the network.
  • • Secure: This blockchain is significant because it is open to all users. A larger variety of records come in enormous sizes.
  • • Anonymous Nature: You can join without disclosing your name or identify, making it a secure platform for your transaction.
  • • Decentralized: Each user has a copy of the ledger; there is no single platform that manages the network.

Disadvantages

  • • Processing: As a result of its magnitude, the transaction procedure moves at a fairly slow pace. The procedure of verifying each node takes a long time.
  • • Energy Use: Producing a proof of work requires a lot of energy. To join the network, quality computer hardware is required.
  • • Acceptance: Governments are forced to cope with the difficulty of incorporating technology more quickly since there is no centralized authority.

Private Blockchain

These blockchains are not as dispersed as the public blockchain, it is more secure than the others because only a minor number of nodes can contribute in the process. These are less transparent than a public blockchain. They are only accessible to specific authorized users. On a private network, these blockchains function. In this, only a small number of people are allowed to join a network inside a company or organization shown in Figure 3.

Figure 3. Private blockchain network

Advantages

  • • Speed: The rate is high because the transaction is so small. Confirmation of each node requires less time.
  • • Scalability: The scalability can be changed. The network's size can be by hand selected.
  • • Privacy: The level of privacy has increased as a result of rising commercial expectations for confidentiality.
  • • Balanced: The transaction is more balanced because it is only accessible by a small number of users, which improves network performance.

Disadvantages

  • • Security: This type of node is rarer, thus there's a chance that someone may alter it. There are greater security dangers with these blockchains.
  • • The difficulty of building trust is one of its main problems as a result of centralization. Businesses can use this technique to punish wrongdoing.
  • • The blockchain system as a whole could be in jeopardy if any nodes go offline due to the limited number of nodes.

3. Hybrid Blockchain

It is a mixture of private and public blockchain content, where some portions are under the authority of a single company and others are made openly accessible. It combines blockchains that are both public and private. Both permission and non-permissioned systems are used.

Despite being the owner of this blockchain, a major entity cannot alter a transaction. Smart contracts enable users to acquire information shown in Figure 4.

Figure 4. Hybrid blockchain network

Advantages

  • • Ecosystem: The hybrid character of this blockchain is its greatest strength. The network cannot be hacked because 51% of users are not connected.
  • • Due to the fact that just a small number of nodes verify transactions, they are cheap. Because not every node performs the verification, the computational cost is reduced.
  • • Architecture: It offers a great degree of adaptability while upholding integrity, security, and transparency.
  • • Operations: It has the power to choose which blockchain users to include and whose transactions should be made available to the public.

Disadvantages

  • • Effectiveness: Not everyone can put a hybrid Blockchain into practice. Additionally, the business has certain issues with maintenance efficiency.
  • • Transparency: Someone could choose to hide some information from the user. It depends on the organization whether it will give access to someone requesting it via a hybrid blockchain.
  • • This blockchain ecosystem is lacking incentives for network membership because of its closed ecosystem (Barde, 2022).

Consortium Blockchain

It is a novel approach that satisfies the demands of the company, which also sends or receives transactions, validates the transaction. It is also known as Federal Blockchain. It’s a novel approach as how it addresses the organization's needs. A part of it is both public and private. This blockchain is managed by multiple organizations shown in Figure 5.

Figure 5. Consortium blockchain network

Advantages

  • • Speed: Verification is quick because there aren't many users. Organizations can use this more readily because of the fast speed.
  • • Authority: It can be dispersed at every level and involve multiple entities. Decentralized power increases security.
  • • Privacy: The checked blocks' information is hidden from the general public. But everyone who uses the blockchain can access it.
  • • Flexible: The blockchain's degree of adaptability varies greatly. Due to the decision's small size, it can be made more rapidly.

Disadvantages

  • • Approval: The procedure is less flexible because it has the support of all the members. Since one or more entities are engaging, there might be differences in the vision of interest.
  • • Transparency: The company could be hacked if it becomes corrupt. Organizations may hide information from users.
  • • Vulnerability: This blockchain is more likely to be vulnerable if a few nodes are compromised.

BLOCKCHAIN AND BITCOIN TRANSACTIONS

A bitcoin transaction is the transfer of bitcoin from one address to another. For the transaction to be regarded legitimate, the sender must sign it.

Accounts do not exist with Bitcoin. Instead, Bitcoins of any size are all linked to a specific address that is managed by the bitcoin's owner. They are referred to as Unspent Transaction Outputs (UTXOs).

Each Bitcoin transaction is published to me pool, where it is treated as “pending.” A transaction is regarded as confirmed once it has been included in a block by a miner (Evans, 2014).

Initializing the Blockchain

Initializing blockchain requires the first-ever block to come into being curated manually. Remember, the block should comprise all the characteristics of the said chain. Then the features are shared through network nodes. Moreover, a JSON format file is created for defining the block. There are numerous parameters like Nonce, and Timestamp, which have to be specific. When the JSON file is further filled in, businesses could create folders that comprise the blockchain and the initialization.

Choosing the Right Consensus Protocol

Distributed systems utilize consensus methods to make sure that every node in the system agrees on a specific value or state. A few of the key comparisons between the various consensus protocols are as follows:

  • • Proof of Work (PoW) vs. Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT): BFT and PoW are two of the most used consensus techniques. PoW is often utilised in networks without permission, whereas BFT is typically used in networks with permission. Unlike PoW, which relies on a large number of nodes, BFT relies on a limited number of trusted nodes to validate transactions. Blocks must be mined using a lot of computational power in PoW, whereas BFT does not.
  • • Proof of Work (PoW) as opposed to Proof of Stake (PoS): In networks without permission, PoS and PoW are both employed. PoW needs nodes to execute a particular amount of computational labour in order to validate transactions, whereas PoS requires nodes to stake their own coin as collateral. PoS offers a lower entry barrier and is more energy-efficient than PoW.
  • • Raft vs. Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT): BFT-based consensus systems used in permissioned networks include PBFT and Raft. In comparison to Raft, PBFT is more fault-tolerant and depends on a higher number of nodes to validate transactions. Compared to PBFT, Raft is simpler to use and comprehend.
  • • The Difference Between Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) and PoS: Is that DPoS uses a smaller group of nodes—referred to as delegates—to validate transactions. The network chooses the delegates, and the more cryptocurrency a node invests, the more voting power it has. Although DPoS is less decentralised than PoS, it is faster.
  • • Federated Byzantine Agreement (FBA) in Comparison to Proof of Stake (PoS): FBA is a consensus technique used in permissioned networks that depends on a group of nodes that trust one another to confirm transactions. Although FBA requires greater node trust than PoS, it is more fault tolerant.

Generally, the choice of consensus protocol is determined by the unique needs of the network, including the required degree of decentralization, network size, and desired amount of fault tolerance.

Proof of Work (PoW) Permission-less Majority of nodes Low Medium Low High Cryptocurrency networks

Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) Permissioned Larger set of trusted nodes High Medium High Very High Financial systems, government networks
Raft Permissioned Leader-based High Fast Medium Medium Distributed databases, cloud systems

The blockchain allows the first member of the network to produce the answer to write the following block. Additionally, this enables routine writing of the blocks. The consensus process also guards against hacking and spam attacks.

  • • Insurance companies lose a lot of money as a result of fraudulent activity. It is expensive and difficult to identify fraudulent activity involving data from both public and private sources.
  • • Blockchain can also automatically check claims made by third parties. Additionally, it can use personal gadgets to automatically validate payments. Insurance companies can consult blockchain-stored transactions.

Management That Is Compartmentalized

Selling and managing insurance policies requires a significant amount of labor. The insurance industry must also deal with an intense rivalry, bureaucracy, and traditional methods.

Blockchain's cutting-edge ledger and intelligent contracts are combined to enable seamless processing. A single trustworthy technology can help the payout procedure cut down on time-consuming delays.

Most significantly, blockchain is changing the foundation of the insurance sector. It promotes the need for ongoing innovation and helps people break free from strange traditions. Customers need the cost flexibility, speed, and transparency that blockchain can deliver.

Healthcare

Healthcare is the most undervalued sector in the global economy, although it outperforms all other verticals in terms of revenue generation. Everyone is now aware of how crucial it is to have a strong healthcare facility thanks to historically difficult periods like COVID-19. Blockchain opens up fresh possibilities in the health sector. For instance, it makes sure that patient data is stored. Blocks can be used to transport electronic health records for storage purposes. All of the information from tens of thousands of patients can be kept in the ledger. The technique also permits complete information duplication and storage with excellent encryption as a backup.

By making the replacement, any prospective DDoS attacks are further eliminated from precedent. Hackers cannot modify or delete health records using blockchain.

Blockchain Tech in Healthcare Can Initiate

Drug Monitoring

Blockchain technology can significantly reduce the problem of product counterfeiting. In some networks, transactions between distributors and manufacturers were simple to track. The system would make it simple to verify authenticity, track momentum through time, and quickly learn about makers.

Electronic Health Records

The single-most patient registry is considerably created by blockchain. Higher security standards, dependable operation, and remote accessibility are all provided by EHR. Patients typically worry about data synchronization, but the infrastructure makes it possible. Once patients give their consent, doctors can easily evaluate the whole medical history using blockchain. The strategy would drastically lower clinic hardware expenditures. As soon as data is updated in real-time, processing will cease. Doctors will be able to quickly learn specifics about blood types, allergic reactions, and chronic conditions.

Standardization

Blockchain technology enables the use of EHR and conventional protocols. Additionally, blockchain greatly facilitates the establishment of global standards for patients.

Blockchain technology might enable efficient operation at what appears to be a minimal cost in healthcare and medical facilities.

Real Estate

A significant part of global income and assets come from real estate. Real estate is a significant means to earn an income due to the transactional nature of the industry. Independent networks are now widely used in the real estate industry. Blockchain offers advantages like tokenizing real estate assets; processing industry fundamental operations efficiently; reducing costs associated with automation processes; granting access to assets distributed globally; creating investor-specific pools due to the fractionalization of total ownership; gaining access to secondary market opportunities; and increasing data accessibility and transparency.

THE THEORY OF ELECTRONIC MARKETS

The Theory of electronic markets is based on the research done by economists Ronald Coase and Oliver Williamson, both of whom have won Nobel Prizes. Why do we see businesses in a free market economy, wondered Coase? One purported advantages of the free market economy is that, it “self-regulates,” but in practice, we frequently see situations when management directs economic activity rather than the economy acting on its own. In order to resolve this paradox, Coase pointed out that using the price system had cost, and that for particular types of economic activities, those costs were larger in the market than in a corporation (Benson, 1989).

As a result, we would anticipate seeing few economic activities occurring within enterprises and few other occurring within markets.

By imagining a make-or-buy choice, Williamson operationalizes Coase's concept. A company can either purchase a component from the market or manufacture it internally to employ in its own production process. Williamson provides a thorough explanation of the circumstances that could influence a decision to make or buy. For our instantaneous goals, it is crucial that private economic activity occurs either in the enterprises or in the hierarchical structure, i.e., firms. Transaction costs are a major factor in determining where that economic activity occurs.

Malone argues that computers and information technology have significantly lowered the cost of processing and transferring information. outlining three potential implications on industrial organization. An improvement in communication efficiency that has a beneficial influence on markets and hierarchies is the first definition of an “electronic communication effect.”

AN ORGANIZING ELEMENT

Any civilization had to deal with the economic issue of distributed information. Because of this, it was unknown which resources did society had access to, what further uses they may have, and what prices had to be established in the market since they were not just handed. This understanding was crucial in the context of the argument between socialist economists, particularly Oskar Lange and Ludwig von Mises, and F.A. Hayek, and that raged in the 1930s. In the absence of market pricing, opportunity costs, according to Mises, could not be determined, and resource allocation would therefore be inefficient. Lange had retorted that market prices might be either computed using econometric approaches or simulated through an accounting process. No central planner could ever have access to enough information to perform the computations Lange envisioned. This was Hayek's contribution to the discussion. Furthermore, Mises maintained that even if central planners had all the essential data, they would not be as motivated to make wise judgments as businesspeople. The socialist calculation controversy has now been settled, but Mises' and Hayek's arguments are still crucial. In 2003, What is the relation between decreasing communication costs over time and the economics of various decision-making structures? is Malone's restatement of the original hypothesis. Now he makes the case with respect to centralized vs. decentralized decision-makers, rather than advocating for a choice between hierarchies and markets. He outlines the elements that will influence the decision between decision-making frameworks, which is crucial for our objectives.

These three components are motivation, trust, and decision information.

He contends that IT can increase reliability through greater monitoring, likeness, and socialization of remote decision-makers.

According to Sundararajan, trust have five indicators in a digital environment which are: prior interactions, peer experience learning, blazing, digitised social capital, and external authentication. He also made the crucial argument that the later two indicators, digital social capital, and outside authentication Networked services which can offer these cues at scale have grown significantly and quickly.

BLOCKCHAIN AS A FOUNDATION FOR THE ECONOMY

Similar to how industrialized energy was distributed at scale during the industrial revolution, industrialized trust will be distributed at scale during the digital revolution.

Following the industrial revolution, the industrial organization saw a shift from U-form organization to the M-Form organization, according to Chandler. We envision the establishment of a “V-form” organization with the industrialization of trust (Allen, 2016).

Organization in V-Form

The V-form organization will be made up of number of completely autonomous businesses that work together as if they were a single vertically integrated company, using blockchain technology to coordinate and audit tasks that were previously handled by the corporate office or by the market. A future digital economy would have a trading infrastructure provided by these V-form companies. Currently, economic infrastructure includes not only the legal framework and social norms that support commerce and economic activity, but also the physical infrastructures like ports, highways, rails, and other similar facilities. It is simple to envision an additional digital (blockchain) layer of economic infrastructure that both supplements and replaces current forms of economic infrastructure in a world where trust has been industrialized (Allen, 2011).

A future digital economy would have a trading infrastructure provided by these V-form companies. Currently, economic infrastructure includes not only the legal framework and social norms that support commerce and economic activity, but also the physical infrastructures like ports, highways, rails, and other similar facilities. It is simple to envision an additional digital (blockchain) layer of economic infrastructure that both supplements and replaces current forms of economic infrastructure in a world where trust has been industrialized. The Aragon Network is an example of a V-form organization; virtual organizations can be built as a collection of smart contracts, and the network offers a mechanism for resolving disputes. This organization can be characterized as decentralized and fully congruent with the concept of the electronic market.

On the other hand, “centralized” V-form organizations are also visible. An example would be the Tradelines platform that IBM and Maersk created. Here, traditional hierarchical organizations have given way to a V-form organizational structure.

BLOCKCHAIN ANARCHY AND PRIVATE GOVERNANCE

Through DAOs, A blockchain-based economic system can automate and carry out smart contracts entirely, however there is still a problem with contractual enforcement, especially given that these voluntary contracts may not be approved by a centralized authority and are thus not always carried out in secret. Noting that private agents may desire property of not being observable by the government may be the source of the efficient advantage, since it would allow one to avoid government predation in relation to taxes, regulations, or other constraints. This is comparable to instances where private ordering principles emerge on their own in anarchic or shadowy economies.

CONCLUSION

According to Malone, a dramatic rearrangement of the industrial organization will result from information technology commencing in the late 1980s. Costs of communication have decreased. Viable business models started to appear in the second half of the 20th and the first decade of the 21st centuries. The major internet platforms we use today were founded at that time. This is an example of the electronic brokerage effect. We still haven't seen the electrical integration effect in operation on a significant scale. The electronic markets theory is based on the cost of trust, not a general decrease in communication costs. We might infer that blockchain technology offers the structure for digital.
